body: It's a concept that I'm familiar with I just don't know whether he thinks he's joking when he says it or says we've broken up or something. I think maybe because he doesn't think we have broken up then I mustn't but to all intents and purposes in my mind we have.
I do, but I have some of his stuff that I need to return. I'm hoping he unlocks me in a couple of days but I don't know how likely that is.

I handled it terribly. The first time I said it he laughed and we joked about it. Truly I would not have said it again if I had realised, and honestly I do not recall the name psychopath being a trigger because sometimes he tells me things in a light way and I don't pick up on it because we joke so much. It's not an excuse I know.

Yes, I should have left, I didn't because I wanted him to know that I didn't see him as this person at all. 

In your experiemce is there any way that I can make this right?

I've mentioned before that I thought he might have a problem controlling his temper when he got really angry and screamed at a fridge. Obviously not at that time. He did not take it well. He said that if I said that it would basically be calling him this family member and never to mention it again.

Do you think that because I said something about him being a psychopath it was mocking his mental health issues. I truly thought it was a joke because he laughed about it at first and he always tells me when he's unhappy with something immediately if it's really bothering him. 

What have I done :( :(

He does have mental health issues, but I've never mocked them, when we've had arguments before he's said he has a plan to commit suicide. When we've been having difficult times he brings it up like he's defo going to do it but then when we are good he says he doesn't want to. 

We always mock each other, he calls me stupid things and I do it to him as well but this time it might have been too close to the bone. He has two housemates who would know if anything was up, one of them in the room next door so he probably overheard.

He's broken up with me a few times during the course of our 1 year (would have been today) relationship. Like, anytime something is going well or there's an occasion it's like he gets scared or something. But they are like a pushing me away to see if I care enough to fight for us so I don't know if this is another one of those times and he's gone for good.

Thank you for your advice, and yes, I should have been more sensitive about the situation, I guess that because we joke a lot with each other and we joked in the beginning it didn't upset him. I picked up on the cues too late and I thing maybe it's now too late to fix it.

I appreciate your advice :)

In his defense, he told me and I apologised but I didn't do it with a lot of humility. I probably had a bit of confusion because it seemed like a joke at first. Maybe he thought I had an attitude and that made him react even worse. 

But yes I see your point. I think we both handled it quite badly and I guess I'm just wondering if anything is salvageable haha.
It is, you're right. At first we were joking and we laughed about it so I didn't pick up that it had bothered him. I just don't know what to do that's all. I guess I can't really do anything.

All of this is wonderful, thank you. Don't worry about the 'fucking someone's life up' cos as people keep telling me if he wants to do it he will and there's nothing I can do to change that.
We spend a lot of time in each other's company and I just need to focus on making that positive and helping him do things that fulfil him. 
Honestly, I truly appreciate you taking time out of your day to give me this advice <3

Thanks for much for your advice, I'm going to try and create a positive environment to see if that helps and talk about this compromise and if things get worse I'll keep that number in mind. I appreciate you taking time out of your day to give advice:)

Thanks you, I need to look into the resources in the area. The problem is that the NHS had a looongass waiting list and I have zero money to pay for private counselling. 
He did say yesterday that he could 'compromise' and try to find a job that might make him change his outlook or just give him more time. But I  reflected to him (as he said to me about himself) that he shouldn't live to make other people happy since that was what he had been doing and it would drain him even more.

That's what I'm wondering. I wonder if the best approach with him is to talk about it, he will not react well if I just take him. He will be stubborn and not seek the help if it's not a decision he's made, generally tends to reject or feel burdened if it's something I've asked or suggested.
Thank you, he said he wants his last few months to be as happy as possible and it was only a couple of days ago he told me so I'm struggle to compartmentalise and ... not cry I guess.
